description: Process a Freedom of Information Act request from intake through document search, review, redaction, and response.

steps.description: Receive and log the FOIA request with tracking details.

inputs.name: foia-request
inputs.desc: The incoming request with requester name, description of records sought, and preferred format

inputs.name: agency-foia-rules
inputs.desc: Agency-specific FOIA regulations, fee schedules, and timelines

outputs.name: logged-request
outputs.desc: Request logged with tracking number, receipt date, and statutory deadline

outputs.name: scope-assessment
outputs.desc: Preliminary assessment of which offices hold responsive records

process: Log the request with a tracking number and the date received.
Calculate the statutory response deadline (20 business days, or 10 for expedited).
Identify which offices or systems likely hold responsive records.
Send the acknowledgment letter to the requester.

steps.description: Search for and collect responsive documents from identified sources.

outputs.name: collected-documents
outputs.desc: All potentially responsive documents gathered from the identified sources

outputs.name: search-log
outputs.desc: Record of searches performed, systems queried, and date ranges covered

process: Send search taskers to each identified office with the request scope.
Search electronic systems (email, file shares, databases) for responsive records.
Collect the returned documents and log the search methodology.

steps.description: Review documents for responsiveness and apply exemption-based redactions.

outputs.name: reviewed-documents
outputs.desc: Documents marked responsive, non-responsive, or partially responsive with applied redactions

outputs.name: exemption-log
outputs.desc: Log of each redaction with the exemption cited and a brief justification

process: Review each document for responsiveness to the request.
Apply redactions under applicable exemptions (b1 through b9) with documented justification.
Mark each page as released in full, released in part, or withheld in full.
Log every redaction with the exemption number and reason.

steps.description: Assemble the response package and send to the requester.

inputs.name: exemption-log
inputs.desc: Redaction justifications for the response letter

outputs.name: response-package
outputs.desc: Response letter, released documents, fee assessment, and appeal rights notice

outputs.name: foia-case-record
outputs.desc: Complete case file with request, search log, review notes, response, and metrics

process: Write the response letter with page counts (released in full, released in part, withheld, non-responsive).
Include the exemption citations for any withheld or redacted material.
Calculate and assess any applicable fees.
Include the appeal rights and send the package.
Close the case file with all documentation.

description: Develop a regulation from proposed rule through public comment, analysis, and final rule publication.

steps.description: Draft the proposed rule with regulatory analysis.

inputs.name: policy-objective
inputs.desc: The problem being addressed and the desired outcome

inputs.name: authorizing-statute
inputs.desc: The statutory authority for the rulemaking

outputs.name: proposed-rule-text
outputs.desc: Draft regulatory text with preamble explaining the basis, purpose, and expected impact

outputs.name: regulatory-impact-analysis
outputs.desc: Cost-benefit analysis, small business impact, and paperwork burden estimate

process: Draft the regulatory text with clear definitions, requirements, and compliance dates.
Write the preamble explaining the statutory authority, problem, and proposed solution.
Prepare the regulatory impact analysis (costs, benefits, alternatives considered).
Include the small business flexibility analysis and paperwork reduction act estimate.

steps.description: Publish the proposed rule for public comment and manage the comment period.

inputs.name: regulatory-impact-analysis
inputs.desc: Analysis to publish with the rule

outputs.name: public-comments
outputs.desc: All comments received, categorized by issue and commenter type

outputs.name: comment-summary
outputs.desc: Summary of comment themes, frequencies, and notable submissions

process: Publish the proposed rule in the Federal Register with the comment period and submission instructions.
Collect comments through the designated channels (regulations.gov, mail, email).
Categorize comments by issue, for/against, and commenter type (industry, public, other agency).
Summarize the comment themes and identify issues requiring response.

steps.description: Analyze comments and draft responses for the final rule preamble.

outputs.name: comment-responses
outputs.desc: Written response to each comment theme explaining agreement, disagreement, or change made

outputs.name: rule-changes
outputs.desc: Changes to the proposed rule based on comments, with rationale

process: Address each significant comment theme with a substantive response.
Identify where comments warrant changes to the proposed rule.
Draft the revised rule text incorporating the changes.
Document the rationale for accepting or rejecting each suggested change.

steps.description: Finalize the rule and publish in the Federal Register.

inputs.name: comment-responses
inputs.desc: Responses to incorporate in the preamble

outputs.name: final-rule
outputs.desc: Published final rule with preamble, comment responses, regulatory text, and effective date

outputs.name: rulemaking-record
outputs.desc: Complete record of the rulemaking process for the administrative record

process: Assemble the final rule document with updated preamble and comment responses.
Set the effective date (minimum 30 days after publication for major rules).
Submit to the Federal Register for publication.
Compile the administrative record (proposed rule, comments, analyses, final rule).

description: Track legislation from introduction through committee, floor action, and enactment for an organization monitoring relevant bills.

steps.description: Identify and filter bills relevant to the organization.

inputs.name: policy-interests
inputs.desc: Topics, keywords, and committees relevant to the organization

inputs.name: legislative-session
inputs.desc: Congressional session or state legislature session to monitor

outputs.name: tracked-bills
outputs.desc: Bills flagged for monitoring with summary, sponsors, and committee assignment

outputs.name: priority-classification
outputs.desc: Each bill classified as high, medium, or low priority based on potential impact

process: Search newly introduced bills by keyword, committee, and sponsor.
Review each bill summary and classify by relevance to the organization's interests.
Assign a priority level based on potential impact and likelihood of advancement.

steps.description: Track the progress of each bill through the legislative process.

outputs.name: status-updates
outputs.desc: Latest action on each bill (committee hearing, markup, floor vote, conference)

outputs.name: amendment-tracker
outputs.desc: Amendments filed, adopted, or rejected that affect the organization's interests

process: Check each tracked bill for new actions (committee schedules, votes, amendments).
Record the latest status and any changes to the bill text.
Flag amendments that change the bill's impact on the organization.

steps.description: Analyze the potential impact of advancing legislation on the organization.

outputs.name: impact-assessments
outputs.desc: Analysis of how each advancing bill would affect the organization if enacted

outputs.name: legislative-tracking-report
outputs.desc: Weekly or monthly report of all tracked legislation with status, impact, and recommended actions

process: Analyze the current text of each advancing bill for operational and financial impact.
Identify compliance requirements, timelines, and costs if enacted.
Recommend organizational actions (comment, testimony, operational preparation).
Compile the tracking report with status, analysis, and recommendations.

description: Run a government procurement from requirements through solicitation, evaluation, and award.

steps.description: Define the procurement requirements and prepare the solicitation document.

inputs.name: procurement-need
inputs.desc: What is being procured and why

inputs.name: funding-source
inputs.desc: Appropriation, grant, or fund paying for the procurement

outputs.name: requirements-document
outputs.desc: Statement of work or specifications with evaluation criteria

outputs.name: solicitation-package
outputs.desc: Complete solicitation (RFP, RFQ, or IFB) with terms, timeline, and submission instructions

process: Write the statement of work or performance specifications.
Define the evaluation criteria and their relative weights.
Set the procurement timeline (posting, questions, proposals, evaluation, award).
Assemble the solicitation package with all terms and conditions.

steps.description: Publish the solicitation and manage the question and answer period.

outputs.name: published-solicitation
outputs.desc: Solicitation posted to required venues with proof of publication

outputs.name: qa-amendments
outputs.desc: Questions received, answers published, and any amendments to the solicitation

process: Post the solicitation to required venues (SAM.gov, agency website, trade publications).
Collect vendor questions during the Q&A period.
Publish answers and any resulting amendments to all prospective vendors.
Close the solicitation at the stated deadline.

steps.description: Evaluate proposals against the stated criteria and select the best value.

inputs.name: qa-amendments
inputs.desc: Any amendments that changed requirements or criteria

outputs.name: evaluation-results
outputs.desc: Each proposal scored against the criteria with strengths, weaknesses, and risks

outputs.name: selection-recommendation
outputs.desc: Recommended awardee with documented rationale

process: Convene the evaluation panel and review the criteria.
Score each proposal independently on technical merit, past performance, and price.
Consolidate scores and document consensus strengths, weaknesses, and risks.
Identify the best value and document the selection rationale.

steps.description: Execute the contract award and handle the debriefing period.

outputs.name: executed-contract
outputs.desc: Signed contract with the awardee

outputs.name: procurement-record
outputs.desc: Complete procurement file with solicitation, proposals, evaluation, award, and debriefing records

process: Issue the award notice to the selected vendor.
Notify unsuccessful offerors and offer debriefings.
Execute the contract and record the obligation of funds.
Compile the complete procurement file for audit.
